# Everything you need to build a world

> Author it once. Fill it with people. Run it live. Playbox is one surface for the whole arc — the tool that designs the experience is the same tool that runs it, in any place you point it at.

[See it live](/playbox/showcase){primary}
[See pricing](/playbox/pricing)

## Author the world
The view is the edit. There's no separate build mode — you shape the world while you're standing in it, and the people in it with you shape it back.
- Describe what you want in plain language; the system drives every screen, light, and speaker to match
- Compose spaces from parts that snap together
- Co-authorship is the default, not a multiplayer add-on
- A two-person crew ships what used to take a full production team

## Bring real places in
Capture a real space and walk through it — photorealistic, fast, no manual modelling. The look that tells everyone this is real.
- Turn a phone capture into a navigable space
- Real rooms carry their own light and depth
- Set the scene, then author the moment on top of it

## Living media, not files
Everything coming into and out of your world — camera, video, audio, sensors — is a live part of the scene. A world is the thing happening in it; it doesn't go to disk and come back.
- Drop a camera and every viewer sees it instantly
- Feeds and inputs are first-class scene material
- The world lives, responds, and remembers

## The audience is in it
Presence, movement, and gesture become inputs. Viewer becomes participant becomes player — the audience isn't a seat, it's an instrument.
- The crowd's energy shapes the space in real time
- A sub-125ms loop: walk in and you're already part of the show
- Show fifty is shaped by show one — returning fans get callbacks, and the world knows them

## One world, every place
A world isn't bound to one room. Beam it between places, broadcast it online, or run it in a living room — reach never depends on a big install.
- The same world can play a club night and a couch
- Beam links places, so two crowds can share one moment
- Publish to a venue, a stream, or a home from the same surface

## Yours, all the way down
Native on Windows and macOS, on commodity hardware. Your world is your own — and so is everything it generates.
- Runs on a $1,500 mini PC
- Your world is its own database, in your own region — self-host it, move it, hand it off, or archive it
- Open and interoperable — no vendor lock-in, and the data your world generates belongs to you

## A team of agents
Agents work alongside you as real collaborators — they hold roles, build in parallel, and do the work that scales so you can do the work that doesn't.
- Agents build and respond in the world like people do
- Take on a bigger show without a bigger crew
- You direct; the fleet executes
